summary: Claiborne County, Tennessee, lookout registered 2014 as US 991 and administered by the Division of Forestry; no build date, design, staffing or visit record found.

events.note: Registered March 14, 2014 as US 991, TN 12; nominated by Ron Stafford

evidence.supports: administered by Tennessee Division of Forestry
Springdale tower in Claiborne County at 2300 ft
most TDF towers built late 1940s to about 1960
evidence.quote: the majority of the TDF's fire lookout towers were constructed during the period between the late 1940s and ca. 1960

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register gives 2,283 ft (696 m) and the Landforms list gives 2,300 ft for a Springdale tower in Claiborne County. Neither source explains the 17 ft difference, so both figures appear in the story and the gap is left open.

sources.title: Tennessee Division of Forestry Fire Lookout Towers
sources.publisher: National Register of Historic Places multiple property document, National Park Service (npgallery.nps.gov)

notes_for_editor: Only the Register registration page and one Landforms row say anything specific. No build date, design, staffing, visit report, or access rule was found in readable sources. Two Facebook posts from the Clinch-Powell History page came up in search with claims about an early 1950s build date and radiological monitoring for Oak Ridge; neither page could be opened, so the claims are unverified and are not in the story. Check them before anyone adds them. The brief's 'NGS None' register entry was not checked.
